question: Which of the following best defines school health according to the provided text?

options.A: A program strictly focused on treating injuries sustained during sports
options.B: A comprehensive set of procedures and services to promote the well-being of students and staff
options.C: The administration of first aid exclusively by teachers in the classroom
options.D: A purely academic curriculum focused on biology and human anatomy

explanation: School health is defined as a comprehensive set of procedures, programs, and services implemented within a school to promote and improve the physical, mental, and social well-being of all pupils, students, and staff members. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h1)

question: Why is understanding school health particularly important for nursing students in Nigeria?

options.A: It allows them to take over teaching responsibilities from classroom instructors
options.B: It helps them mitigate communicable diseases and support vulnerable populations undergoing critical growth
options.C: It guarantees elimination of all infectious diseases in Nigerian communities immediately
options.D: It is a requirement exclusively for working in tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Nursing students must understand school health because the school environment houses a vulnerable population facing rapid growth, allowing nurses to proactively mitigate communicable diseases common in classrooms and foster resilient communities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h1)

question: What is one of the primary objectives of a school health program regarding academic performance?

options.A: To increase school fees for health maintenance
options.B: To reduce absenteeism caused by preventable illnesses
options.C: To replace standard classroom instruction with medical lectures
options.D: To eliminate the need for general hospitals

explanation: A core objective of school health programs is to reduce absenteeism caused by preventable illnesses, which in turn improves academic retention and educational outcomes. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h2)

question: How do schools function within the broader public health landscape according to the text?

options.A: As sentinel sites to monitor public health trends and contain outbreaks
options.B: As exclusive manufacturing plants for pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: As primary taxation centers for local health boards
options.D: As permanent isolation camps for chronically ill adults

explanation: Schools serve as sentinel sites where public health trends can be monitored, allowing rapid identification and containment of outbreaks like measles or cholera. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h2)

question: What are the three traditional foundational pillars of a comprehensive school health program?

options.B: School health services, healthful school environment, and school health education
options.C: Tuition management, sports coaching, and administrative discipline
options.D: Community policing, sanitation tax, and political engagement

explanation: The traditional foundational pillars of a comprehensive school health program are school health services, a healthful school environment, and school health education. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h3)

question: Which of the following falls under the psychosocial aspect of a healthful school environment?

options.B: Protecting students from bullying and emotional stress
options.C: Providing a safe piped water supply

explanation: The psychosocial climate of a school environment focuses on protecting students from bullying, harassment, and undue emotional stress. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h3)

question: What is a primary risk associated with inadequate water supply and poor waste disposal in schools?

options.A: Increased prevalence of waterborne diseases like cholera and typhoid
options.B: Immediate reduction in standardized test scores
options.C: Higher rates of visual and hearing impairments among students

explanation: Inadequate water supply and poor sanitation lead to the spread of waterborne diseases such as cholera, typhoid, and dysentery among students. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h4)

question: Why are separate and functioning handwashing stations equipped with soap important in a school setting?

options.A: To replace the need for physical education classes
options.B: To encourage proper hygiene practices after toilet use and before eating
options.C: To serve as decorative elements for school inspections
options.D: To function as primary drinking water points for students

explanation: Handwashing stations with soap encourage proper hygiene practices, helping to prevent the transmission of infectious germs after using the toilet and before meals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of conducting routine medical screenings, such as visual acuity tests, in schools?

options.A: It permanently cures all genetic disorders in children
options.B: It catches conditions early, preventing misinterpretation of health issues as poor academic aptitude
options.C: It eliminates the need for any further community health outreach
options.D: It provides schools with direct funding from international pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Routine screenings catch conditions like undetected eye problems early, preventing them from being mistakenly labeled as poor academic aptitude and ensuring timely intervention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h5)

question: Which of the following clinical activities is typically part of school health services?

options.A: Performing major orthopedic surgeries in the classroom
options.B: Administering routine immunizations and catch-up campaigns
options.C: Prescribing long-term psychiatric medications without medical supervision
options.D: Conducting dental extractions using standard carpentry tools

explanation: School health services successfully deliver immunization catch-up campaigns and routine vaccines, such as HPV and tetanus boosters, directly to the student population. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of integrating health education into the school curriculum?

options.A: To ensure health knowledge is actively translated into lifelong healthy behaviors
options.B: To prepare every student to specialize exclusively in nursing or medicine
options.C: To eliminate practical science experiments from the classroom
options.D: To fill empty teaching schedules with non-academic activities

explanation: Curriculum integration ensures that health education is actively translated from theoretical knowledge into lifelong healthy behaviors for the students. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h6)

question: Which topic is considered an essential component of adolescent health education within the school curriculum?

options.B: Puberty changes and menstrual hygiene management
options.C: Hospital budget allocation and facility management

explanation: Adolescent health education addresses critical milestones such as puberty changes and menstrual hygiene management for girls, alongside mental health and STI prevention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h6)

question: How do school feeding programs positively impact educational outcomes according to the text?

options.A: By replacing all classroom learning hours with cooking classes
options.B: By providing a reliable nutritious meal that improves concentration and serves as an incentive for attendance
options.C: By forcing students to purchase processed fast food from external vendors
options.D: By eliminating the need for physical education and sports

explanation: School feeding programs provide a nutritious meal that enhances concentration, prevents mid-morning lethargy, and serves as a strong incentive for school enrollment and attendance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h7)

question: What is an important supportive public health intervention often paired with school nutrition programs?

options.A: Routine deworming exercises to enhance nutrient absorption
options.B: Mandatory fasting days for all enrolled students
options.C: Complete prohibition of water consumption during school hours
options.D: Replacement of school meals with synthetic vitamin pills only

explanation: Deworming exercises are frequently paired with nutrition programs because intestinal parasites hinder nutrient absorption in children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h7)

question: What is the primary role of the school nurse within a comprehensive school health framework?

options.A: Managing school financial accounts and student tuition payments
options.B: Acting as a clinician, educator, advocate, and liaison between school, family, and healthcare centers
options.C: Instructing students exclusively in mathematics and physical education
options.D: Constructing physical school infrastructure such as classrooms and boreholes

explanation: The school nurse functions comprehensively as a clinician, educator, advocate, and liaison connecting the school, families, and primary healthcare delivery systems. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h8)

question: Why is teacher participation crucial in the identification of student health issues?

options.A: Teachers possess advanced medical degrees in pediatrics
options.B: Teachers are legally required to prescribe medication in the classroom
options.C: Teachers spend significant time with students and can spot subtle changes in behavior or energy for timely referral
options.D: Teachers manage the national health ministry budget for schools

explanation: Because teachers spend considerable time with students daily, they are well-positioned to observe subtle changes in health or behavior and make prompt referrals to the nurse. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h8)
